entries.reason: IV dose/indication and contraindication context require an exact authoritative product source before a rule is created.
Do not import the user-written haemostatic dose without an authoritative SmPC and exact indication.
Strength, route and local product identity must be verified. Antihistamines must not delay IM adrenaline in anaphylaxis.
Steroid dosing is indication-specific; no routine anaphylaxis first-line rule is encoded.
Dose depends on indication and product. Lemod-Solu must never be treated as sodium bicarbonate.
No 'hypoallergenic' label is accepted; exact parenteral product and indication require review.
Seizure treatment is route-, age- and scenario-specific and requires a dedicated authoritative rule.
Exact treatment context and route must be source-backed; it is not auto-linked to every metoclopramide adverse effect.
Acidosis/hyperkalaemia use requires indication- and laboratory-specific rules; no universal ampoule dose is encoded.
5%, 10%, 20%, 50% and other concentrations are different products and indications. D5W is not encoded as a diuretic for hypertension or as default resuscitation fluid.
0.9% bolus amount is patient- and indication-specific; no universal 500-1000 mL rule is encoded.
Ringer, Ringer lactate/Hartmann and other balanced crystalloids have different compositions.
Antibacterial dosing belongs in the antimicrobial source-first pipeline and must not be duplicated in acute-care data.
Source-backed azithromycin regimen candidates already exist in the DRX antimicrobial pipeline; reuse them rather than duplicating rules here.
Indication-, route- and anaerobic-infection-specific dosing belongs in the antimicrobial pipeline.
Sepsis is not a sufficient standalone dosing indication; antimicrobial source and renal context are required.
Cefuroxime axetil oral and cefuroxime sodium parenteral formulations are not interchangeable; exact paediatric product is required.
Exact marketed formulation and strength are required before any dose is encoded.
Do not infer an ophthalmic combination from separate products; exact label and ocular indication are required.
Variable multi-ingredient composition and strength by manufacturer.
Dose and route depend on diagnosed deficiency/indication and exact product; wellness claims are not dosing indications.
Exact product/indication required. It is not encoded as a routine method to discontinue diazepam.
Formula varies by product; no universal tablet dose is modeled.
Exact strain(s), CFU, formulation and product evidence are required.
Supplement/product formula and age-specific label must be verified before use.
Exact product identity and ingredient list are required; ivy/plantain/Althaea/thyme must not be inferred from the name.
